history.changes: Written as an App, People: who may do what, its kinds of record, the who-can-do-what screen, its doors and rules. No definition changes; what is approved is the App itself.

Who may do what, as data: a role is a named set of rights; a membership puts a person in a company with a role between two dates; a mandate lets an office keep a client's books within a scope of rights; a substitution hands a person's rights to a deputy between two dates; a group names a set of people for a supervisor's reach. The pack's roles: owner, chief accountant, accountant, reader, support. The view that shows who can do what, every right opening to the grant that gives it.
A person can say their given name, family name and birth date — what a natural person's tax return needs.
The person as master data: who acts, who is assigned work, who stands in when they are away.

description: People: the person as master data — who acts, who is assigned, who stands in — and who may do what: roles, memberships, mandates, substitutions, groups. Market-neutral; every pack that assigns work builds on it. v3: rights as data (DIRECTION 2026-10-19, People and rights).

citations: every ERP keeps the people who use it as master data: a user with a role, and a substitute for absence (SAP workflow substitutes, Comarch operators)
every event in Rhea already names its actor; a person is that actor as an object, so cases, notifications and disputes can refer to a human the way documents refer to a contractor

KSeF 2.0's rights ladder: the taxpayer holds every right, grants named rights to people and to an authorised entity (the accounting office) with or without the right to pass them on; the office grants its employees rights in the client's context — Rhea's membership, mandate and role are those three
the right to manage rights is never implied by the right to do the work (KSeF: zarządzanie uprawnieniami is its own grant): a wildcard over doors stops at the people domain
